sections.title: Three-word phrasal verbs
sections.content:
Advanced three-word phrasal verbs for fluent English:
• come up against — face a difficulty. We came up against unexpected resistance from the council.
• look forward to — anticipate with pleasure. I'm looking forward to the summer holidays.
• get away with — avoid punishment. He broke the rules but got away with it.
• cut down on — reduce the amount. Doctors advise cutting down on sugar and salt.
• live up to — meet expectations. The film didn't live up to the hype.

sections.title: More advanced phrasal verbs
sections.content:
Phrasal verbs for sophisticated expression:
• do away with — abolish or eliminate. The company did away with unnecessary paperwork.
• make up for — compensate for. She worked extra hours to make up for lost time.
• stand up for — defend a cause or person. He always stands up for what he believes in.
• go back on — break a promise. You can't go back on your word now.
• get on with — continue doing something. Stop complaining and get on with your work.

exercises.question: To meet expectations or standards is to live up ___:
exercises.explanation: Live up to means to fulfil expectations.

exercises.question: To eliminate or abolish something is to do away ___:
exercises.explanation: Do away with means to abolish or put an end to.

exercises.question: To avoid being punished is to get away ___:
exercises.explanation: Get away with means to escape blame or punishment.

exercises.question: To reduce your consumption of something is to cut down ___:
exercises.explanation: Cut down on means to reduce the amount or quantity of.

exercises.question: To break a promise is to go back ___:
exercises.explanation: Go back on means to fail to keep a promise.

exercises.question: To compensate for a loss is to make up ___:
exercises.explanation: Make up for means to compensate for something.

exercises.question: To defend a person or principle is to stand up ___:
exercises.explanation: Stand up for means to defend or support a person or principle.

exercises.question: To face a difficulty or obstacle is to come up ___:
exercises.explanation: Come up against means to be faced with or opposed by.
